title: An Evaluation page and Models tab: measures, confusion matrix with a cutoff slider, and curves
request: There is no evaluation part in Models or the sidebar: all the evaluation of the model, precision, recall, F1 and the other important things, and a confusion matrix; plot like the report's charts.
spec: The final stage recorded the holdout metrics, six cutoffs and calibration bins, but kept no scores, so no ROC, precision-recall or confusion matrix could be drawn; the holdout is read once.
plan: A core module that turns scores and answers into measures, confusion counts at 51 cutoffs and curves (counts only)
The final stage keeps it for the holdout read it makes and for the validation folds
For older projects, give back exactly what their record allows: the confusion counts from the recorded cases, alerts and true positives
One panel builder for a sidebar page and a Models tab, legends outside the charts

decisions.decision: Older projects are not scored again: their page is read back from the record, says so, and has no ROC or gains.
decisions.why: The holdout is read once; a second read would break the rule the whole product stands on.

decisions.decision: The page is built in the app's own chart kit, with the legend beside each chart, never inside it.
decisions.why: The report the owner showed had labels lying over lines and a per-class chart drawn as a line over class numbers.

decisions.decision: The cutoff the person moves changes the matrix and the measures; the model is never refitted.
decisions.why: A cutoff is a decision about use, not about training.

change: dclab_core/model_evaluation.py (new), studio/engine.py (_evaluation, evidence.evaluation), routers/projects.py (GET evaluation), web/src/evaluation.js (new), views/evaluation.html (new), views/models.html (Evaluation tab), core.js (nav, icon), look.css (matrix), features.js, build.py, scripts/browser_e2e.py (20 pages), tests/test_model_evaluation.py.

findings.defect: No evaluation part: no precision, recall, F1 or confusion matrix anywhere in the app.
findings.scenario: The person opened Models and found a ranking of families and a holdout number; nothing said what the model gets right and wrong.
findings.cause: The final stage kept a few numbers and six cutoffs, and no scores.
findings.fix: The stage keeps the evaluation; the page and tab show it; an older record gives back its exact counts.

findings.defect: A text in the matrix's wrong-answer cells was unreadable on the darkest red.
findings.scenario: A false-negative cell with a large share: its small labels were grey on red.
findings.cause: The heat classes set a background only.
findings.fix: The cells from the third step on use the text colour.

measurements.name: Evaluation on the owner's real project
measurements.gate: the confusion counts add up to the rows and match the recorded precision and recall
measurements.result: 1,600 rows: 1,470 true negatives, 7 false positives, 117 false negatives, 6 true positives, from the record alone
limits: one project; no ROC, gains or histogram for a record made before the scores were kept

measurements.name: Three new projects, binary, multiclass and regression, in the browser
measurements.gate: each kind's panels draw and the slider moves the matrix
measurements.result: the binary page has 12 measures, 7 charts and a comparison with the validation folds; the cutoff 0.20 changed the matrix from 10 to 42 false positives; the multiclass page has its matrix and class table; the regression page its two charts
limits: small invented tables with five stages in quick mode

outcome: A person sees what the model gets right and wrong, on the held-back cases and the validation folds, and moves the cutoff to see the trade.
lessons: A number recorded with the cases and the alerts can give its confusion matrix back exactly: record counts, not only rates.
risks: A project made before this change shows the measures and counts, not the curves, until a new final stage runs for it.
